keyVerseText: And the LORD said unto him, Go, return on thy way to the wilderness of Damascus: and when thou comest, anoint Hazael to be king over Syria:
rootMeaning: The name חֲזָאֵל (Chăzâʼêl) derives from the Hebrew root חָזָה (châzâh), meaning to see, behold, or perceive, combined with אֵל (El), meaning God. Literally, it means "God has seen" or "one who sees God." This etymology conveys a profound sense of divine vision or revelation, implying not only physical sight but also spiritual insight or prophetic perception, which enriches the simple English gloss by emphasizing a relationship between seeing and God’s active involvement.
usageInScripture: The word חֲזָאֵל occurs 23 times in Scripture, primarily referring to Hazael, a king of Syria. It is most commonly translated as "of Hazael" or "against Hazael," indicating possession or opposition related to this figure. The consistency in translation underscores the historical and narrative role of Hazael as a significant political and military actor, especially in relation to Israel and Judah, as well as his interactions with the prophet Elisha.
theologicalSignificance: Understanding חֲזָאֵל as "God has seen" invites reflection on God’s sovereign oversight and providence even in the lives of foreign rulers. The name suggests that God’s vision and judgment extend beyond Israel to the nations, fulfilling His purposes through historical events. This reminds believers that God's sovereignty is comprehensive, and His plans unfold through human history, including the rise and fall of kings. It also points to the theme of divine revelation and prophecy, as Hazael’s life intersects with the prophetic ministry of Elisha, highlighting God’s control over earthly powers for His redemptive will.
keyVerseReflection: In 1 Kings 19:15, God commands the prophet to anoint Hazael as king over Syria, emphasizing divine appointment and oversight. The name חֲזָאֵל here reinforces that this king’s rise is not random but seen and ordained by God. This underscores the truth that God is actively involved in history, even appointing rulers who will impact His covenant people. The meaning "God has seen" deepens the understanding that God’s vision encompasses all events, and His sovereignty directs the course of nations according to His divine plan.
